Learning to Code With GenAI: CS1-LLM
sources.text: Search this site Embedded Files The CS Ed Research Lab CS Education Research Lab at UC San Diego CER Lab Mission The CS Education Research (CER) Lab explores ways to improve outcomes for all students interested in studying computing. Our recent efforts include proposing and evaluating new pedagogies, using machine learning to identify struggling students, designing assessments to measure learning, uncovering the source of student struggles, and creating new course structures to improve sense of community. CER Research Seminar Open to anyone interested in CS Education Research! In the Winter 2026 quarter, we will be meeting on Thursdays from 11am-12pm (room & Zoom link TBD). For students, you can enroll in CSE 294 to receive credit for this seminar. Current Projects Code in Academia & Industry Project Lead: Anshul Shah My work aims to develop pedagogical approaches to address the academia-industry gap. Specifically, I aim to identify and address students’ struggles related to program comprehension, code quality, and use of LLM tools while working with large code bases. CS Ed for Latine Students Project Lead: Ismael Villegas Molina The focus of my research is to enhance computer science education for Latine students. I am currently working on this through culturally relevant methodologies. My ongoing projects involve 1) developing and assessing culturally relevant materials for introductory CS courses, incorporating diverse Latine cultures (e.g., Mexican, Peruvian, Guatemalan, Brazilian, etc.) to a racially/ethnically diverse classroom, and 2) gathering insights from CS professors at Minority Serving Institutions on their culturally relevant teaching strategies. Previously, I conducted a comprehensive literature review on efforts to support Latine students in computer science and explored the use of Generative AI for crafting culturally relevant materials, assessing its effectiveness in reflecting Latine cultural elements. Additionally, I implemented bilingual Spanish-English computer science instruction for high school students, analyzing its impact on learning outcomes. Learning to Code With GenAI: CS1-LLM Project Lead : Annapurna Vadaparty Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot are reshaping computing education, especially in introductory programming courses (CS1). These tools solve traditional assignments and exams, challenging what is taught and assessed. As professional engineers adopt LLMs, preparing students to use them is essential. To address this, we developed an LLM-integrated CS1 course ( CS1-LLM) for UCSD's introductory CS course . This course shifts focus from syntax mastery and coding from scratch to skills like explaining and testing code and breaking down problems into prompts for LLMs. We seek to understand how students can best learn in the new LLM-assisted learning environments, and find out how to best support students with computing fundamentals of the LLM era. Student Engagement Project Leads: Audria Saravia Montalvo & Alex Chao With the rise of Generative AI (GenAI) in a post-COVID educational landscape, student engagement in their courses has drastically shifted. Anecdotally, instructional staff in the Computer Science and Education (CSE) department have noticed a decrease in student interactions with both their peers and course staff. However, there has been limited work done to quantitatively analyze engagement trends in computing courses and qualitatively understand student sentiments and experiences. Our project aims to understand how student engagement has changed in the last several years and address how instructors can improve student engagement in future courses. Interested in Joining? Undergraduate students are welcome to apply to join the CER lab through the Early Research Scholars Program . Graduate students are welcome to apply to join the CER lab through the UCSD Computer Science & Engineering Department Graduate Admissions . We are currently looking for new graduate students in the 2025-2026 application cycle (applicants interested in enrolling in Fall 2026). sources.text: Previous Next Humanity-Centered Design In the universe of academic disciplines, we see connections instead of divisions. Humanity-centered design at the UC San Diego Design Lab transcends disciplinary boundaries and charts new frontiers in design research, education, and practice. Our mission is to foster design-driven transformation by educating design leaders, imagining alternative futures, and equipping people and communities with the knowledge, tools, and opportunities to address the most pressing societal challenges. Attend our Master of Design Info Session! The UC San Diego Master of Design is a two-year graduate program for designers ready to move from making things to shaping systems, and from contributing to leading. Register for the Virtual Info Session News Stay in Touch! Subscribe to the Design Lab Mailing List . Visit Us The Design Lab is located on the third floor of the Design and Innovation Building (DIB) at UC San Diego . The west entrance is across from the Epstein Family Amphitheater , and the east entrance is next to the UC San Diego Central Campus Station bus and trolley stop. Directions and parking .
